### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **37** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`  _(via /:object/export (route, bridged from symbol templateMode — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via /:object/export (route, bridged from symbol templateMode — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `607f8f1d76ada72f290b089ca8cd74e6847d4a85` — the merge of head `78f7e31e401aeaedf6288138c0eb7812aea50751` into base `121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 607f8f1d76ada72f290b089ca8cd74e6847d4a85 && git checkout 607f8f1d76ada72f290b089ca8cd74e6847d4a85
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f 78f7e31e401aeaedf6288138c0eb7812aea50751 && git checkout -B drift-repro 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f && git merge --no-ff 78f7e31e401aeaedf6288138c0eb7812aea50751

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `78f7e31e401aeaedf6288138c0eb7812aea50751`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line on the changeset and the PR body is true and complete against the diff. New CLI flags `--lang zh|en` and `--prompt short|detailed`. New on `./runner` from `prompts.ts`: `PROMPT_LANGS`, `PromptLang`, `PROMPT_LENGTHS`, `PromptLength`, `PromptChoice`, `MissingLanguageError`, `promptLanguageGaps`, `promptLanguageRefusal`, `statedPromptChoice`, `promptChoiceText`; from `driver.ts`: `samePromptChoice` and `RecordedDriver.assertPromptChoice`. A new optional trailing `choice` parameter on `buildPrompt`, `iteratePrompt`, `templateIteratePrompt`, `questionPrompt`, `operationPrompt`, `runHalf` and the `RecordingDriver` constructor. New optional fields `RunOptions.promptChoice`, `CardRun.promptChoice` (outside the strict `counts`), `Recording.promptChoice` and `CardScorecard.promptChoice`. No existing export is removed or narrowed; every existing call keeps its result.

The answer that moves is declared and is confined to runs that pass a flag. With neither flag `text` returns `en ?? zh` and the build turn gets `prompt.detailed`, and no record, scorecard or recording carries a choice (pinned; the thread also compared every prompt of all 9 library cards against main by sha256). With `--lang`, every card-authored text a prompt renders is sent in that language only; the runner's wrapper and the card's plain strings it quotes stay English, as the README says. A card lacking a text the run's modes would render is skipped by the CLI before any scaffold, naming each missing field, and `runCard` refuses it too, so no path silently falls back. `--prompt` changes the build turn only. A recording carries the choice, and a replay under another is refused before any card runs (`samePromptChoice` treats an absent build prompt as `detailed`, and an absent language as distinct from an explicit one, which is the strict side). Design point 6 was checked before building: on `leave_balances` a Chinese reply with the right figures grades correct and cited and a Chinese decline passes the unanswerable question (pinned), so `src/score/**` is untouched.

### ② Semver level

Patch, as the changeset bumps it. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no spec key, app metadata or card JSON changes. The widening is additive exports, optional fields and optional trailing parameters of the evaluation package `@objectstack/scenarios`.

### ③ Boundary flags

None. No `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path, no platform runtime or security behaviour. No grader verdict moves: grading is the unchanged `gradeCardAnswer`.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-xdvo2j`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qiby1cctpVpRbJzjccvY`

**VERDICT: PASS**
